title: The ℓ¹-Bass Conjecture for Discrete Groups
main_claim: For every discrete group G and idempotent e in M_q(ℓ¹(G)), the Hattori–Stallings trace is zero on all but finitely many conjugacy classes, and every class where it is nonzero consists of finite-order elements. This is the ℓ¹-Bass conjecture in the finite-support form of Berrick–Chatterji–Mislin.
coverage:
I read all seven sections in full and checked each main step by hand.

(1) Reduction (Sec 2). I verified the holomorphic idempotent formula p = 1/2 + (a − 1/2)(1 − b)^{-1/2}. I also verified the identities u − I = (p − e)(2e − 1) and ue = pu. The weighted-norm convergence giving an exponential moment holds. Passing from Γ back to G only merges conjugacy classes.

(2) Cyclic trace formula (Sec 3). The bijection between tuples and increments, total weight equal to τ, and the deletion identity from p² = p all hold. The canonical connection Σ x_i dt_i has Pfaffian (−1)^m. The transgression argument works: rotation acts on the (n−1)-simplex with orientation sign −1, so I = −I. I checked the factorial normalization.

(3) Channels (Sec 4). The center-geometry diameter bound of 4r holds. The selector concentration bounds hold in both cases, as do the exponential parameter choices. The Fisher bound C ε^{-2} d is independent of the support size, via the normalized-vector derivative and the e^{γr − 0.04N} estimate. The early-radius domination E_r ≤ E_{6r} holds. I checked the Hoeffding constants, the log-sum-exp derivative bound 11/(10r), and the Gibbs string concentration and Fisher bound. The product Fisher identity holds, as does the averaging-drop inequality.

(4) Connection (Sec 5). I verified that U' = 2(δ_0 − ρ) for both final kernels, and the contraction identity. Telescoping gives C_j ≥ Φ_j − Φ_{j+1} − 30ε_j, with radii matching in both the early and later versions. The raw-stage bound C_0 ≥ 1/5 − Φ_1 holds. In case (ii) the final lag terms vanish because S ∩ gS = ∅. The terminal multiplier gives W C_{b*} ≥ Φ_{b*}, and the face, rotation and centralizer compatibilities hold.

(5) Curvature (Sec 6). The skew kernel pairing (dB_j)_{ii'} = <X_i, T X_{i'}> holds, as does the compression Pfaffian bound via Hadamard. I checked the Hilbert–Schmidt exponent arithmetic δ_j^{-1/2} δ_{j+1}^{1/4} = n^{1/4} β_j^{-1/8}. The order-kernel rank approximation and the orbit and three-shift block decompositions give s_ν ≤ C/ν. The raw-entry bound 2 l_i l_{i'}/R and its support bound 2R/n hold. In the occupancy lemma I checked the order-statistics argument, the cell comparison, the Hölder/multinomial step, and the bound (1 + k/m')^{k/4}. The averaging over raw subsets is legitimate because the number of completions does not depend on I_0. The entropy bound S^{n/2} and partition count S^n hold, and the small bases are R^{-1/8}, R^{-15}·polylog and R^{-40}·polylog.

(6) Conclusion (Sec 7). R is fixed depending only on M_p, then n → ∞, so the order of limits is correct. The bound of 4r on conjugacy length gives finitely many surviving classes.

As a plausibility check I tried to build counterexamples from averaging idempotents over finite subgroups. Those idempotents have surviving classes of conjugacy length O(M_p), which is consistent with the theorem's radius r ~ M_p^{10+}. I did not numerically simulate the constructed connection.
